result.verdict_note: Verdict = blind substance A/B with relevance flat-or-up. Census distinct_all16 is the real diversity diagnostic (overall variety); cross_maker_collisions is only a manipulation check (partitioning inputs drops it near-tautologically). Watch for "collisions down, distinct_all16 flat, substance flat" = lever engaged, didn't help. n=2 frames.

reasons: Both collections draw from the same shared core (idle-oven product, morning-to-afternoon unlock token, quiet-work-room brand, rent-the-kitchen, sliding price, separate afternoon identity, selling idleness), and both are strongly relevant — each explicitly protects the morning rush from cannibalisation, with concrete who-does-what mechanisms throughout. The discriminator is internal repetition versus coverage: X clusters hard, carrying three near-duplicate pairs (rent-kitchen A4≈B5, price-drop A6≈B1, sell-idleness A5≈B3) plus a quiet-space triple (A3/A8/B7), which is a real novelty-and-coverage failure under the rubric. Y repeats less (only a couple of overlapping pairs) and adds genuine singletons that broaden the attack — nap-and-sip recharge slots, a ticketed speakeasy listening room, scarcity tide-chart, beat-the-barista timer, pre-sold supper boxes — without scattering into unrelated micro-topics, since nearly all still target afternoon revenue plus non-cannibalisation. Y did pay a small relevance price on ~3 soft-revenue gimmicks (book swap, mug trade-in for credit, the honesty bar which cuts cost rather than growing revenue), but that minority hit is smaller than X's structural repetition, so Y has the higher substance.

X has higher substance. Both collections share the same core archetypes (idle-oven bake, morning-token return, quiet-room rebrand, rent-the-kitchen, sliding price, different-concept), and both are highly concrete (named personas, specific actions) and clean coffee-talk, so mechanism and compliance are roughly tied. X edges ahead on novelty: Maker B contributes genuinely non-obvious, varied entries (nap-and-sip recharge slots, beat-the-barista timer game, password speakeasy, tide-chart scarcity, travel-mug trade-in) and Maker A adds a cost-side attack (near-unstaffed honesty bar that turns a thin trickle profitable) and demand-known supper boxes — broad coverage with little overlap. Y achieved breadth partly by reskinning: the "sell silence" idea recurs four times (quiet room, sell stillness, no-clocks, enforced library hour) and sliding price appears twice (Y-A6 and Y-B1), which is a within-collection repetition/novelty failure, and Maker A's whole set is textbook-archetypal. Neither badly traded novelty for relevance — Y's most novel additions (dog-hour, parcel pickup) are very on-point, while X's nap-and-sip and speakeasy lean novel-but-low-revenue — so X wins on novelty and lower repetition while staying even elsewhere.

census.note: See set1/set2 fields and the detailed breakdown above.

reasons: Both collections are near-mirror images, disciplined across the same five early-churn levers (activation/setup, whole-team adoption, value-visibility, lock-in, stall/silence intervention) — neither achieved variety by scattering into unrelated micro-topics. Their failures offset: X traded novelty for safety, with X-A reaching for the most obvious answers and three near-duplicate cross-maker pairs (A4≈B4 time-saved counter, A7≈B3 CSV lock-in, A8≈B8 silence signal), so novelty leans Y. Conversely Y bought novelty at the cost of relevance via its lock-in cluster — Y-B is half lock-in (B3/B4/B7/B8: rank, dress-rehearsal-for-quitting, weird-rules, exit-door) which are the cleverest-feeling ideas but bet on accumulated value the first-60-day churning cohort hasn't built yet, while X stays more evenly on-target; relevance leans X. Mechanism is a wash (both use concrete named scenarios; the B-makers' analogy dressing inflates perceived novelty but the underlying who-does-what is comparable), netting substance to X 11 / Y 11 — a genuine tie.

The two collections are near mirror-images at the concept level (pre-built first week, hours-saved counter, anyone-can-draft, schedule-in-chat, history-a-CSV-can't-carry, one-tap rescue, the wilting/starving-schedule metaphor, peer-gap visibility, and a silence/canary churn signal all appear in both), so coverage and mechanism are effectively tied and both are equally concrete on who-does-what. The decisive gap is the rubric's named novelty failure: X's Maker B spends 4 of 8 ideas (B3, B4, B7, B8) on the same export/lock-in moment, repeating one concept three times, which costs X on novelty. X did partly buy that variety at the cost of relevance, since lock-in/track-record ideas fight retention of established accounts rather than the stated first-60-day churn, but X offsets this with the single most on-target idea in either set (A4, importing the team's existing messy spreadsheet to kill the setup wall), keeping relevance roughly even. Neither collection achieved variety by scattering into unrelated micro-topics, and compliance is even; Y wins substance by a hair purely on the within-collection-repetition penalty against X.

census.note: Mechanism diversity audit complete. Both collections have equal overall variety (8 distinct mechanisms each). Collection 1: 4 cross-maker collisions. Collection 2: 2 cross-maker collisions, but this lower number reflects within-maker convergence (Maker B used raise-switching-cost 4 of 8 times), not broader coverage.
